properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-16, in his words: *"should reflow2 somehow enforce (or at least tell the agent) that design artifacts must be done in some recognized standard (IFC in terms of architecture; not sure for other domains??) — trying to drive that if my brother (Alex) uses this to design his shop/garage; how can we assume that whatever the agent creates will deliver something that is a recognized standard... this needs to be a question from the very beginning for any domain that reflow2 is used — I imagine that in some domains, there is no recognized standard or tools-of-the-trade, but it should still try from the beginning."*

⭐ THE POINT IS THE MOMENT, NOT THE LIST. He is not asking reflow2 to know every domain's standard. He is asking that the QUESTION be put at the start of every project, and that its answer — including "there is none" — be a recorded fact the design can read, so that an agent producing an HTML plan sheet (bhome, 2026-08-31) or an .stl for a building is caught by the design rather than by a planner.

═══ WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY HOLDS ═══
· EnvironmentRule already has rule_type `standard` with `authority` ("a standards body (ISO)") and COMPLIES_WITH / VIOLATES edges — the vocabulary for "this project's artifacts follow IFC" exists today and nothing asks for it.
· Project.domain is written and never read (req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted) — the anchor the question would hang from is stored and unused.
· genesis and adopt each run an opening interview; neither asks what the domain's artifacts are expected to be, so the answer is never recorded and no detector can miss it.
· Artifact.artifact_type (code / spec / drawing / model / …) says what KIND a file is, never which STANDARD it conforms to.
· req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off (accepted) is the licensure half; this is the format half, and they are different: a file can be in the right standard and still need a stamp, or be stamped and unreadable by any tool.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
A. ⭐ ASK AT THE BEGINNING, RECORD THE ANSWER, NOTICE ITS ABSENCE — the three legs this design has learned a discipline needs. (1) genesis and adopt ask: "what standard do design artifacts in this domain follow, who issues it, and what tool checks a file against it?"; (2) the answer lands as an EnvironmentRule(standard) the Project COMPLIES_WITH — or a recorded "none known" so silence is not mistaken for an answer; (3) a detector reports a project with domain artifacts and no declared standard, and an Artifact realizing a domain capability whose format is outside the declared one. ⚠️ Cost: "format" needs a home on Artifact (a `standard` or `format` property), and the detector can only judge by declared format, never by opening the file — reflow2 does no file I/O.
B. A SEEDED TABLE — reflow2 ships a small map from domain to standard and checker (architecture → IFC / IfcOpenShell; mechanical → STEP / a CAD kernel; electronics → KiCad or Gerber; systems engineering → SysML v2 or UAF; software → none, the code is the artifact) as a default the interview offers. ⚠️ Counter, and it is req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted's own: a default nobody chose reads as a choice; and dec:idea-who-warrants-a-domain-template asks who keeps such a table current. Offer as a suggestion the person confirms, never as an answer.
C. ENFORCE AT THE TOOL — link_artifact refuses a domain artifact whose format is not the declared standard. ⚠️ Counter: the standard is often the OUTPUT (IFC, STEP) and the reviewable source is something else (a FreeCAD script, OpenSCAD); refusing the source would forbid exactly the artifact the who-authors reframing says the agent may write. Notice, do not refuse.
D. NOTHING NEW — the agent is expected to know the domain. ⚠️ Counter: bhome is the measurement against this. The agent knew architecture has standards and drew an HTML sheet anyway, because nothing in the design asked.

═══ THE HONEST LIMIT ═══
reflow2 can record that a project's artifacts must be IFC and can notice a file that is not; it cannot itself check that an IFC file is valid IFC. That check is a Verification with an executable form (an external validator run by the agent or a CI step), and its result comes back as evidence — the same shape as every other check here. What this idea adds is that the question gets asked, the answer gets stored, and its absence gets noticed.
properties.name: OPEN — should every project, from genesis or adopt onward, name its domain's recognized standard for design artifacts and the tool that checks them (IFC for architecture, STEP for mechanical, …), or record that none exists — and should an artifact outside that standard, or a project that never said, be noticed?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, nothing promoted. His framing is close to intent ("this needs to be a question from the very beginning") and it is recorded as an idea only because promotion is his word, not the session's. The three-legs shape (a typed home, an instruction at the start, a detector for absence) is used because this design has measured twice that a vocabulary with fewer legs never reaches a user's project. Kept separate from the who-authors idea: that asks who writes the artifact, this asks what the artifact must be — and the second question is answerable for a domain before anybody is chosen to write anything.
